We achieved a significant reduction in dispatch turnaround time this quarter.

I have consistently maintained high quality standards throughout my career.
The carrier delivered fifteen containers to the logistics hub this morning.
We need to schedule a brief meeting to discuss the new corporate policies.

The vendor confirmed that raw material supplies will arrive as scheduled.
Please verify that the bank reconciliation statement matches the ledger balance.
Our team organized the warehouse layout to optimize picking and packing speed.
I took the initiative to resolve the discrepancy between physical stock and ERP counts.
The customer requested an expedited delivery for the urgent export order.
We must ensure complete compliance with international maritime shipping standards.
Thank you for considering my application for the Operations Lead role.

minimal_pairs.sentence: He drank fine wine while inspecting the grape vine.
minimal_pairs.tip: For /v/, touch upper teeth to lower lip. For /w/, round your lips like an 'oo' sound.

minimal_pairs.sentence: The logistics manager was very wary of unexpected transport delays.
minimal_pairs.tip: Do not bite your lip for 'wary'; keep lips rounded.

minimal_pairs.sentence: The cargo ship carried fifty sheep across the sea.
minimal_pairs.tip: Short 'i' in ship is quick and relaxed; 'ee' in sheep is longer and smiling.

minimal_pairs.sentence: These safety shoes fit my feet comfortably.
minimal_pairs.tip: Notice how your tongue stays relaxed for 'fit' and arches higher for 'feet'.

minimal_pairs.sentence: Take a quiet sip of coffee while watching the container ship dock.
minimal_pairs.tip: For 'sip' keep tongue tip behind teeth; for 'ship' pull tongue back slightly.

minimal_pairs.sentence: Please take a seat and review this balance sheet.
minimal_pairs.tip: Do not slur /s/ into /sh/.

minimal_pairs.sentence: The export parcel was wrapped in a thin layer of tin foil.
minimal_pairs.tip: For 'thin', put tongue between teeth. For 'tin', tap tongue behind teeth.

minimal_pairs.sentence: I think we should not allow the metal parts to tink together.
minimal_pairs.tip: Breathe gently through tongue and teeth for /θ/.

minimal_pairs.sentence: Do not dare to go over there without a safety helmet.
minimal_pairs.tip: Vibrate vocal cords with tongue between teeth for 'there'.

minimal_pairs.sentence: The wet pavement caused the delivery driver to call a vet.
minimal_pairs.tip: Round lips for wet; bite lower lip gently for vet.

minimal_pairs.sentence: The driver traveling west wore a fluorescent safety vest.
minimal_pairs.tip: Differentiate the initial /w/ and /v/.

minimal_pairs.sentence: The cart wheel squeaked as we transported the veal consignment.
minimal_pairs.tip: Keep lips round for wheel.

minimal_pairs.sentence: The microchip manufacturer will ship the order on Monday.
minimal_pairs.tip: 'ch' has an explosive stop; 'sh' is a smooth continuous flow.

minimal_pairs.sentence: If you catch the early courier, you will receive the cash voucher.
minimal_pairs.tip: Finish 'catch' with a sharp stop.

minimal_pairs.sentence: Use a ballpoint pen to sign for the metal pan delivery.
minimal_pairs.tip: Drop your jaw wider for 'pan' than for 'pen'.

minimal_pairs.sentence: He had a bad back after lifting the heavy bed frame.
minimal_pairs.tip: Jaw drops open wide for 'bad'.

minimal_pairs.sentence: The fuel tank was full so don't be a fool and overfill it.
minimal_pairs.tip: Short relaxed 'u' in full versus rounded long 'oo' in fool.

minimal_pairs.sentence: Please pull the forklift away from the water pool.
minimal_pairs.tip: Relax tongue for pull; tense lips for pool.

minimal_pairs.sentence: We cut the plastic wrapping before assembling the wooden cot.
minimal_pairs.tip: Central open sound for cut; rounded lips for cot.

minimal_pairs.sentence: My heart was relieved that nobody was hurt in the warehouse.
minimal_pairs.tip: Open throat wide for 'heart'; keep lips neutral for 'hurt'.
